match.reason: The closest bank card, Determinants of health, is a broader framework covering individual and environmental factors too, and it does not frame the five named factors as explaining differences in youth health, so no single card matches the brief exactly.

draft.title: Factors affecting youth health
card: Peer group
friends of a similar age. They can influence behaviours such as smoking, alcohol use, physical activity and eating.
Family
family can shape habits, provide support and meals, and model behaviour, which can help or harm health.
Education and income
more education and higher income can give better access to food, housing and health care. Lower levels can limit these.
Health literacy
the ability to find, understand and use health information to make decisions. Higher health literacy can lead to better choices.
draft.remember: Peers, family, education, income and health literacy can all shape a young person's health.

a.q: Jai can read food labels and knows how to find reliable advice about sleep and exercise. Which factor is this?
a.why: Finding, understanding and using health information is health literacy. Peer group is about the influence of friends, which is not the focus here.
a.clue: Focus on understanding and using information.

b.q: Priya's friends all start vaping, and she feels pressure to join. Which factor is most directly affecting her health risk?
b.why: The pressure comes from friends of a similar age, so peer group is most direct. Health literacy could help her resist, but it is not the source of the pressure.

problems.detail: The clue 'Focus on understanding and using information' repeats the card's definition of health literacy almost word for word, so it gives the answer away.
The distractor 'Education level only' uses 'only', an awkward qualifier the card does not use. It marks this option as a throwaway and narrows the real choices.
